VERDICT: DEFECTS

FINDING 1
  location: Facts & Assumptions L9
  severity: nonfatal
  claim: "Ordered-field arithmetic: a positive real has a positive inverse, $0<s\le t$ gives $1/t \le 1/s$, and the order is total and transitive ([[def-ordered-field]], [[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-interval]])."
  evidence: The three cited items are definitions of an ordered field, a complete ordered field, and intervals; none of them states or directly yields the reciprocal inequality. The property is a standard consequence of the field and order axioms but requires an additional lemma (e.g., on inverses and order) that is not cited. The gap is small and a competent reader can fill it in a few lines; therefore it is nonfatal.

BOUNDARY: All boundary cases (p>0 rational, zero endpoint, index shift, forward and reverse directions of the biconditional) are correctly handled; no degenerate or empty scenario affects the claim.

SOURCES: Inspected the full text of all 28 provided cited items. The integral test, p‑series theorem, rational‑power laws and monotonicity, derivative of a power, algebra of continuous functions, etc., support the claims with the noted exception.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered step (1.1–6.1), and Remarks.
